items.statement: Final: explanation of condition switching and α/β selectivity reversal
items.expected: In the final conclusion, explicitly adopt a condition-dependent explanation jointly supported by valid structures, connectivity and competing energies, linking β preference under the β conditions and α preference under the α conditions to the two product connectivities. The authors' phenoxide/cationic switch is a hypothetical reference; alternative explanations with corresponding computational evidence are acceptable. Merely listing two sets of numbers, repeating observations or failing to select a conclusion is insufficient. Exact 45:1, 7:1 or yield reproduction is not required. Do not portray a hypothesized correspondence between conditions and species as a computed complete speciation distribution.

items.statement: Final: distinguish access cost from competition within a state and explain reactivity
items.expected: In the final conclusion, integrate structural/free-energy results for site access with regioselective competition within a state to explain why changes in the coordination environment can affect both reaction facility and selectivity, distinguishing their different physical roles. The authors' reduction of the binding cost by monoxide formation is a reference. A computationally supported connection is required; repeating the two rankings alone is insufficient. Access costs and insertion barriers for models with different compositions, charges or ligands cannot simply be added into a full-cycle barrier. Oxidation/ionization rates or a complete network are not required.

items.statement: Final: use the styrene control to explain bounded substrate dependence
items.expected: In the final conclusion, relate the matched styrene binding and insertion comparisons to the difficulty of reaction of the primary cyclic olefin, providing a model-supported explanation of substrate dependence while preserving the primary reaction identity. One local number or an independent explanation of another substrate is insufficient; do not claim reproduction of experimental styrene yields, exact turnover rates or a universal substrate rule on this basis.
